title: Focus Session Desk — Offline Timer and Task Checklist
customer_problem: People working locally on a desktop need a predictable focus countdown and a small task checklist without accounts, online sync, hidden background activity, or accidental loss of their work.
audience: Students, writers and individual office workers who use a Windows desktop and want a minimal offline session tracker with an immediately understandable first-run experience.
differentiation: Original local-only Tkinter timer paired with a short editable checklist, honest pause/resume/stop behavior, atomic local state persistence and explicit interruption recovery; it is not a notes app or a network productivity service.
scope: Create, edit, reorder, complete and delete a local task checklist with an accessible first-run empty state.
Start, pause, resume, reset and finish configurable focus sessions using a monotonic clock; show elapsed and remaining time without background services.
Persist task and session settings atomically in user-local JSON, with backup and clear recovery or validation messages for damaged state.
When the user exits during an active session, show an honest confirmation and restore an interrupted-session summary without pretending time ran while closed.
Offer Japanese and English UI labels, keyboard-operable primary controls and a usable 1024x768 layout with visible errors and confirmation states.
Provide headless tests for task CRUD, timer transitions, invalid durations, persistence, recovery and restart behavior; never claim Windows GUI PASS without real evidence.
research_note: Untrusted public GitHub issues are weak demand signals, not market proof. The two cited issue URLs were retrieved from distinct repositories. No code/assets from either repository may be copied. This is APP cohort slot 2 of maximum 5, separate from immutable Offline Notes Canary; only candidate research is staged.
